clue.text: Capital city landlords

explanation.surface: A note about property owners in a nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: people who let out city blocks are 'block letters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitals are upper-case print, and the owners who let out urban tower blocks could be called their lessors in a punning second reading.

clue.text: Mandatory work for a bookmaker

explanation.surface: Compulsory labour for someone who takes bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a betting shop, but it means someone who literally makes books.
explanation.definitionFit: A binding rule is compulsory; and a bookmaker here is a maker of books, whose craft includes stitching on covers.

clue.text: Unidentified person's broken nose

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of nose are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A stranger has a fractured nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive of the pronoun for an unspecified person, as in 'to do one's best'.

clue.text: Joint near which suggestive re marks are made

definitions.text: Joint near which suggestive re marks are made

parts.words: Joint near which suggestive re marks are made
parts.note: a finger joint, recalling the idiom for risqué talk that is 'near the' this joint

explanation.surface: A spot where cheeky comments tend to be passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger joint; a risqué joke is said to be near this bony part, meaning almost indecent.

clue.text: Scattered shingle greeted their invasion of these shores

definitions.text: Scattered shingle greeted their invasion of these shores

indicators.note: scattered stones lie in a new arrangement, so the letters of shingle are rearranged

explanation.surface: Invaders landing on a pebbly beach were met by flying stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the Angles and Saxons who landed on British beaches became this people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon settlers, whose name the nation took, arrived by landing on the island's pebbly beaches.

clue.text: Order silence by an expression of scorn

parts.note: by in the sense 'up to' or 'next to', as in pulling a door to
sh is the sound used to demand quiet

explanation.surface: Someone calls for quiet with a sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive exclamation meaning nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Dessert which brings murmurs from the stage

explanation.surface: A pudding that makes the theatre audience mutter.
explanation.walkthrough: Actors playing a crowd say this word over and over to sound like background talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour pink stalk stewed for pudding; extras on stage repeat the word to mimic crowd chatter.

clue.text: It is drawn with two vertical lines

definitions.text: It is drawn with two vertical lines

parts.words: It is drawn with two vertical lines
parts.note: drawn in the banking sense of written out on an account, and marked with two parallel lines so it can only be paid into a bank

explanation.surface: A sketch made with a pair of upright strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank payment order marked with two parallel lines, restricting it to deposit in an account.

clue.text: Iron fire-grate modified for quite the opposite purpose

definitions.text: Iron fire-grate modified for quite the opposite purpose

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters of iron fire-grate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heating appliance is converted to do the reverse job.
explanation.walkthrough: A fire-grate heats; the rearranged letters give the process that cools, the opposite purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooling food or rooms is the reverse of what a grate of burning coals does.

clue.text: Two-rhyme poem? No, a rude composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of no a rude are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A denial that a verse form is a vulgar piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A French verse form built on only two rhyme sounds with a refrain.

clue.text: Guest troubled about body language

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so the letters of Guest are mixed

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for 'concerning', a standard crossword equivalent

explanation.surface: A visitor's anxious posture gives away how they feel.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement of the hands or body that conveys meaning without words.

clue.text: One between sun and earth

indicators.note: the numeral is placed between the outer letters of the sun's name

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something positioned between the sun and our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground or dirt in which plants grow.

clue.text: Hank pushing point into hide

indicators.note: pushing one thing into another puts the compass point inside the hide

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone is driving a sharp point through leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiled length of yarn or thread, the same as a hank.

clue.text: Just a loud melody

parts.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Only a noisy tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable and impartial, as a just decision is.

clue.text: Dickensian gang-leader not out after a cigarette

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
a batter who is not out in cricket is still in

explanation.surface: A villain who has stayed in after lighting up.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is everyday British slang for a cigarette; 'not out' is the cricket term for a batter still batting.
explanation.definitionFit: The fence in Oliver Twist who runs a gang of child pickpockets.

clue.text: Garden trailer that damages the plants

definitions.text: Garden trailer that damages the plants

parts.words: Garden trailer that damages the plants
parts.note: trailer as something that leaves a slimy trail, not a wheeled cart

explanation.surface: A garden cart that crushes the flowerbeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow mollusc that leaves a slime track and eats leaves.

clue.text: Avenger disposed to scratch plate

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of Avenger are set out differently

explanation.surface: A vengeful person is inclined to deface the crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a design into a metal printing plate with a sharp tool.

clue.text: Army carrier giving worker the sack

parts.note: a hand is a manual labourer
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: A military transport gives an employee the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' is read as arm-y: a carrier borne on the arm, not a military transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse carried hooked over the forearm.

clue.text: Pointedly ignoring news items worth keeping

explanation.surface: Snubbing people while clipping the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them deliberately; a press clipping is an article snipped out of a paper to keep.

clue.text: The most prickly of knightly orders

definitions.text: The most prickly of knightly orders

parts.words: The most prickly of knightly orders
parts.note: the Scottish order of chivalry named after a spiky plant emblem

explanation.surface: Which order of knights is the touchiest?
explanation.definitionFit: The spiky Scottish emblem gives its name to the Order of chivalry headed by the monarch in Scotland.

clue.text: Excess weight is what he should fear

definitions.text: Excess weight is what he should fear

parts.note: a glut is an excessive supply
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An overeater ought to worry about piling on the pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy eater is the person most at risk of putting on weight.

clue.text: Cheerful potato slicer

explanation.surface: A happy kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper means bright and lively; a chipper also cuts spuds into French fries.

clue.text: Browning reveals artist taken in by humpback

indicators.note: the artist is held inside the humpbacked animal

parts.note: a camel has a hump on its back
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A Browning poem reveals a painter carried by a camel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' looks like the poet, but it is sugar browning in heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar heated until it turns brown and sticky.

clue.text: East European flogging whip which is a real stinker

parts.note: a Pole is from Poland
the cat-o'-nine-tails, often shortened to cat, was a whip for flogging

explanation.surface: A man from Poland wielding a lash is truly nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel-like animal known for its foul smell.

clue.text: Live the wrong way and you will be so described

definitions.text: Live the wrong way and you will be so described

indicators.note: reading the word the wrong way means taking its letters backwards

explanation.surface: A warning that a sinful life earns a bad name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living wickedly is called wicked or bad.

clue.text: Measure a quarter without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the sound of hesitating is removed

parts.note: a fourth part
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Measure out a fourth part promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of liquid capacity equal to two pints.

clue.text: Nitwit left in bed

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A fool was left lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang term for a stupid person.

clue.text: Very old fashioned Egad!

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped, so the letters of Egad are reformed

parts.note: the reversed run across 'fashioned Egad' is a coincidence; the setter's device is the anagram

explanation.surface: Egad! A quaint old-fashioned oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly, having lived a long time.

clue.text: Former copper carpeted for ill egal junk

parts.note: d stood for the old penny, a copper coin before decimal currency
carpeted suggests covered with a rug, so rug follows

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman is reprimanded for unlawful narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer and 'carpeted' like a reprimand; D was the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk is slang for narcotics such as heroin.

clue.text: How to tie a dangerous captive when very nervous

definitions.text: How to tie a dangerous captive

explanation.surface: Advice on securing a risky prisoner while anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, the way to bind a prisoner firmly; as one word, tense and anxious.

clue.text: Atlasarea of.W. Africa?

parts.note: the question invites a map page but means the north-west African country the Atlas mountains run through

explanation.surface: A question about a region on a map of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingdom in north-west Africa that the Atlas mountains run through; also a fine leather for book covers.

clue.text: Guide's torch for a leading activist

explanation.surface: A guide's lamp for someone at the front of a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp marking a navigable channel; and a prominent figure in a movement.
